significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that TabPFN-like models contain an adjustment signal that "tracks the do-calculus effect across the sign change," responds specifically to confounder availability, and causally moves predictions toward the adjusted answer; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal mechanism. It would establish both the Simpson-flip phenomenon and an internal adjustment mechanism, constraining expected signal trajectories as confounding strength varies and whether model outputs can be interpreted as causal effects rather than predictions; this matters for the broad predictive use case documented by Hollmann et al., "Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model" (Nature, 2025). Verified-false is distinguishable and informative for the tested model class—failure of decoding, selective flipping, and steering would rule out this specified account—but would not show that all scientific foundation models lack causal representations. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not earn this score: the added sign-crossing law, confounder-in/out invariance control, and causal adjustment signal are materially sharper than the median proposal to decode a scientific concept.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Adjustment-Beyond-Observational Index," "Confounder-In-vs-Out Flip Asymmetry," the recovered "adjustment direction," and the proposed "sign-flip/backdoor benchmark" and "probe family." These can function ex ante by auditing a model before causal-effect use and informing the stated "covariate-inclusion policy" or trust gating, although the adjustment direction itself requires model-specific extraction. After recalibration, the criterion predicts a qualitative relation—tracking the do-calculus trajectory and crossing sign near the true threshold—but it does not predict whether a new model will pass or its numerical score; scope is therefore mainly tabular/scientific foundation models and downstream auditors in clinical, drug-response, and omics settings, not foundation models generally. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: removing these concrete audit quantities and the pre-deployment pass/fail consequence leaves only the broad scientific-representation topic, with no comparable transferable handle.
